context.body: When Saul’s son heard that Abner was dead in Hebron, his hands became feeble, and all the Israelites were troubled.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Ishbosheth is murdered in bed; the killers bring his head to David and present the act as divine vengeance, but David answers from prior deliverance and judges them.
observations.label: David rejects another shortcut to the throne: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps Ishbosheth, Rechab, Baanah, Mephibosheth, David, and his men, Beeroth, Mahanaim, and Hebron, murdering, carrying a head, interpreting, recalling deliverance, judging, and burying visible within David's story or later memory.

payload.posture: Read 2 Samuel 4:1–12 as its own judah, conflict, and unification David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places another claimed service to David ends in rejection and punishment inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
